key_reference.title: Association of RIG-I with innate immunity of ducks to influenza
key_reference.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

literature.key_reference_summary: Ducks and wild waterfowl perpetuate influenza viruses with little pathology, and ducks are often resistant to strains that kill chickens. This study shows the RNA sensor RIG-I is present in ducks and clears infection: RIG-I expression is induced ~200-fold early in the innate response of ducks challenged with H5N1 A/Vietnam/1203/04, and transfecting duck RIG-I into chicken DF-1 fibroblasts rescues ligand detection, IFN-beta promoter activity and restricts replication of low- and high-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses. The authors present evidence suggesting RIG-I may be absent in chickens, a plausible contributor to chickens' greater susceptibility. [Summary verified against the published abstract, PMID 20308570; earlier metadata (wrong title/journal/DOI 10.4049/jimmunol.0902471, 'pseudogene' claim) corrected 2026-11-10.]
literature.key_reference_note: verified against PubMed PMID 20308570 abstract; wording: RIG-I may be absent in chickens (NOT a confirmed pseudogene claim)

corpus_quote_for_loss.quote: Chickens (but not ducks) lack the intracellular receptor for viral ssRNA, RIG-I and the gene for an important RIG-I binding protein, RNF135.

literature.llm_profile_overview: DDX58 encodes RIG-I, a cytoplasmic RNA helicase pattern recognition receptor that senses viral RNA and initiates type I interferon signaling during avian influenza infection. In birds, its presence or absence strongly shapes the early innate response to H5N1, with functional RIG-I in ducks associated with rapid interferon induction and control of virus replication, whereas galliform species lack a functional ortholog and show more severe HPAIV disease.
